answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: require cross-attestation from unrelated established identities before a withdrawal clears, because wharf only stays cheap while a closed ring of clones cannot assemble independent attestations without hiring real ones. Concretely, beacon is enforced in the ledger: Every gate is public and recomputable, so honest agents can verify they were treated fairly. Any whisper approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
